title: Exchange along an etale morphism of the target is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $j:V\to Y$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $X_V=X\times_YV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $j_X:X_V\to X$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$, and let $\square_j=(f,f_V,j,j_X)$ be the resulting cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] (bottom map $j$, top map $j_X$). Then for every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] the derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]

$$
 \Ex_{\square_j,K}:j^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf_{V*}\,j_X^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(V_{\Et})$. No hypothesis is put on $f$. (Under the identification of $V_{\Et}$ with the localized site $Y_{\Et}/V$, $j^{-1}$ is restriction to $Y_{\Et}/V$ and $j_X^{-1}$ restriction to $X_{\Et}/X_V$; the lemma says that $Rf_*$ commutes with this restriction, and that the identification is the exchange morphism.)

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma label lemma-restrict-direct-image-open, Tag 0D6G ($(Rf_*E)|_{\mathcal D/V}=Rg_*(E|_{\mathcal C/U})$, proof by a K-injective representative and Lemma lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open, Tag 08FI); with Sites, Lemma label sites-lemma-localize-morphism-strong, Tag 03EF (the underived statement), and the use of both in the proof of Etale Cohomology, Lemma label lemma-base-change-local, Tag 0EZR (literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex), where the restricted base change map is identified with the base change map of the localized square

proof.text: *Step 1 (the square and the restrictions).* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1), applied to $f:X\to Y$ and the object $j:V\to Y$ of $Y_{\Et}$, the base change $j_X:X_V=X\times_YV\to X$ is etale, so $X_V$ with $j_X$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$. The square $\square_j=(f,f_V,j,j_X)$ with the identity of $X\times_YV$ as identification is a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $j$ and $j_X$ are etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] gives natural isomorphisms $\rho_{j,G}:j^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_V$, $G|_V(W)=G(W\to V\to Y)$, and $\rho_{j_X,F}:j_X^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_{X_V}$, $F|_{X_V}(T)=F(T\to X_V\to X)$: under $V_{\Et}\cong Y_{\Et}/V$ and $(X_V)_{\Et}\cong X_{\Et}/X_V$ the inverse images are the restrictions to the localized sites, as in Stacks 0D6G. Applied termwise (naturality), they identify the complexes $j^{-1}P$ with $P|_V$ and $j_X^{-1}P$ with $P|_{X_V}$ for complexes $P$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0D6G (statement: the localized morphism $g:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal D/V$, $U=u(V)$); literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex Section Tag 03S2 ($j^{-1}$ is restriction along $U_{\etale}\to X_{\etale}$)

proof.text: *Step 2 (underived: the exchange along $j$ is an isomorphism, and is the identity of sections).* For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction] gives the isomorphism $\psi_F:(f_*F)|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{V*}(F|_{X_V})$, $\psi_{F,W}=F(c_W):F(W\times_YX)\to F(W\times_VX_V)$ for $W\to V$ etale ($c_W$ the canonical isomorphism over $X$), natural in $F$, and the equality $f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,F})\circ\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}=\psi_F\circ\rho_{j,f_*F}$; hence the underived exchange morphism $\Ex^0_{\square_j,F}:j^{-1}f_*F\to f_{V*}j_X^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism, being a composite of the isomorphisms $\rho_{j,f_*F}$, $\psi_F$ and $f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,F})^{-1}$. This is the underived statement $(f_*\mathcal F)|_{\mathcal D/V}=g_*(\mathcal F|_{\mathcal C/U})$ which the proof of Stacks 0D6G calls clear, citing Sites 03CF/03EF.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0D6G ('it is clear that $(f_*\mathcal F)|_{\mathcal D/V}=g_*(\mathcal F|_{\mathcal C/U})$', citing literature/stacks-project/sites.tex Lemma Tag 03CF and Lemma Tag 03EF)

proof.text: *Step 3 (restriction of a K-injective complex stays K-injective).* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] (with the constant ring $\mathbf Z$, for which module sheaves are the abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]), for the etale $j_X:X_V\to X$ the functor $j_{X!}:\Ab(X_{V,\Et})\to\Ab(X_{\Et})$ is exact and left adjoint to $j_X^{-1}$. So [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], applied with $\mathcal A=\Ab(X_{\Et})$, $\mathcal B=\Ab(X_{V,\Et})$, $u=j_X^{-1}$ and $v=j_{X!}$, shows that for every K-injective complex $I$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] the termwise complex $j_X^{-1}I$ is K-injective. If $I$ is bounded below, so is $j_X^{-1}I$ (termwise functor, $j_X^{-1}0=0$). (Stacks: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 08FI, proved from Derived Categories Lemma Tag 08BJ and the exact left adjoint $j_!$.)

source.place: Lemma label lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open, Tag 08FI, and its proof (Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 08BJ, with the exact left adjoint $j_!$ of restriction); used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0D6G

proof.text: *Step 4 ($\Ex_{\square_j,K}$ is an isomorphism).* Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and let $(I,s)=(I(K),\rho_K)$ be its chosen K-injective resolution, $I$ a bounded below K-injective complex and $s:K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$, so that $Rf_*K=Q(f_*I)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. By step 3, $J:=j_X^{-1}I$ is K-injective, so the identity $\mathrm{id}:j_X^{-1}I\to J$ is a K-injective resolution of the termwise complex $j_X^{-1}I$ (an identity is a quasi-isomorphism). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] to the cartesian square $\square_j$ (step 1), to $(I,s)$ and to this resolution: the termwise underived exchange $\Ex^0_{\square_j,I}=(\Ex^0_{\square_j,I^r})_r:j^{-1}f_*I\to f_{V*}j_X^{-1}I$ is a morphism of complexes, $e=f_{V*}(\mathrm{id})\circ\Ex^0_{\square_j,I}=\Ex^0_{\square_j,I}$, and $\Ex_{\square_j,K}\circ\sigma_{\rm src}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q(e)$ with isomorphisms $\sigma_{\rm src}:Q(j^{-1}f_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{-1}Rf_*K$ and $\sigma_{\rm tgt}:Q(f_{V*}J)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{V*}j_X^{-1}K$. By step 2 every component $\Ex^0_{\square_j,I^r}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves, so $e$ is an isomorphism of complexes (its termwise inverses commute with the differentials), and $Q(e)$ is an isomorphism, $Q$ being a functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence $\Ex_{\square_j,K}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q(e)\circ\sigma_{\rm src}^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(V_{\Et})$. No property of $f$ was used.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0D6G ('Represent $E$ by a K-injective complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$. Then $Rf_*(E)=f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ and $Rg_*(E|_{\mathcal C/U})=g_*(\mathcal I^\bullet|_{\mathcal C/U})$'); literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex proof of Lemma Tag 0EZR (2) (the base change map restricted to $V_i$ is the base change map of the localized square, by 0D6G)

proof.text:
*Step 5 (the identification of the parenthetical remark).* Composing step 4 with the isomorphisms of complexes $\rho_{j,f_*I}:j^{-1}f_*I\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_*I)|_V$ and $f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,I}):f_{V*}j_X^{-1}I\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{V*}(I|_{X_V})$ (step 1, termwise) and using the equality of step 2 in each degree, $f_{V*}(\rho_{j_X,I})\circ e=\psi_I\circ\rho_{j,f_*I}$, one gets
$$\Ex_{\square_j,K}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q(f_{V*}\rho_{j_X,I})^{-1}\circ Q(\psi_I)\circ Q(\rho_{j,f_*I})\circ\sigma_{\rm src}^{-1}.$$
That is: $j^{-1}Rf_*K$ is represented by the restriction $(f_*I)|_V$, $Rf_{V*}(j_X^{-1}K)$ by $f_{V*}(I|_{X_V})$ (the restriction $I|_{X_V}\cong j_X^{-1}I$ being a K-injective complex representing $j_X^{-1}K$, step 3), and $\Ex_{\square_j,K}$ is the class of the identity of sections $\psi_I:(f_*I)|_V(W)=I(W\times_YX)=I(W\times_VX_V)=f_{V*}(I|_{X_V})(W)$; this is the identification $(Rf_*K)|_{Y_{\Et}/V}=Rf_{V*}(K|_{X_{\Et}/X_V})$ of Stacks 0D6G, and it is the exchange morphism.
